text.p: Raytheon Co., which is selling its kitchen appliances unit as part of an effort to focus on defence electronics, Tuesday reported flat earnings for the second quarter.
It earned $209.5 million, or 89 cents a share, vs. year-earlier earnings of $209.4 million, or 88 cents a share.
Sales rose 6.3 percent to $3.32 billion from $3.12 billion.

On Monday, the Lexington, Mass.-company said it was selling its home appliance, heating and air conditioning and commercial cooking businesses for $750 million, transferring the famous Amana and Caloric home appliance brand names to Goodman Holding Co.

The company said its Electronics unit -- Raytheon Electronic Systems, Raytheon E-Systems and Commercial Electronics -- led the increase in second-quarter sales at $1.54 billion, against $1.35 billion a year earlier.
Raytheon Aircraft had record sales of $620 million, up from $544 million in last year's second quarter, but Raytheon Appliances posted sales of $393 million, down from $414 million.
With the sale of its appliance unit, Raytheon exits the business that led to the company's creation in 1922.

The company said it will retain for now its commercial laundry business, which makes Speed Queen coin-operated washers, as well as the electronic controls segment of the appliance group. Last year, these two businesses accounted for 20 percent of the appliances division's sales and 50 percent of its profits.
Raytheon's stock was off 69 cents at $54.19 on the New York Stock Exchange.
